title: Beatrix and the Glasshouse
premise: Yara Voss, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost his sense of taste after a betrayal he has never named, hears an unrecorded song on the radio — one written years ago by his first love, Beatrix, inside the glasshouse commune where they both once lived. The song pulls him into vivid, involuntary relivings of that summer, forcing him to confront the lie he told to survive a fire that destroyed the commune and ruined Beatrix's life. Returning to the crumbling glasshouse before its demolition, Yara must confess what really happened the night of the blaze, trading his reputation, his career, and his last illusions for the truth. In the end, standing in the ruins as the bulldozers arrive, he tastes something again — bitter, real, and finally his own.
about_author: Marguerite Coldharbour is the pen name of a former food writer who spent a decade reviewing restaurants before quietly resigning mid-review. She lives near a decommissioned botanical garden and writes about memory, appetite, and the stories we tell to keep ourselves fed.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He reviews a lavish tasting menu he cannot taste, filing away precise, hollow praise while keeping a private notebook of everything unsaid in his life. The emotional beat is quiet desolation dressed as competence.

chapters.title: Static on the Frequency
chapters.summary: Driving home, Yara hears a song on a late-night radio program — a melody only two people ever knew, never recorded. His POV; the beat is vertigo, recognition arriving like a physical blow.

chapters.title: What the Song Did
chapters.summary: The song triggers his first full sensory flashback: the glasshouse commune at nineteen, heat, tomatoes, Beatrix singing. Yara's POV; wonder laced with dread as the past becomes more vivid than the present.

chapters.title: Beatrix, Briefly
chapters.summary: A secondary POV chapter from Beatrix in the present: she runs a failing seed library in a coastal town, unaware her song is playing anywhere. The beat is guarded resilience.

chapters.title: The Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Yara learns the glasshouse estate is scheduled for demolition in six weeks. His POV; urgency crystallizes into a decision he can't yet justify.

chapters.title: Tasteless
chapters.summary: Flashback structure: the onset of Yara's anosmia after the fire, diagnosed as psychogenic. His POV; grief he refuses to name, doctors offering no cure for guilt.

chapters.title: Return Ticket
chapters.summary: Yara cancels assignments, lies to his editor, and takes the train toward the valley where it all began. His POV; fear disguised as journalistic curiosity.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Him
chapters.summary: Arrival: the village has rewritten its history of the commune, and old neighbors greet him with cold courtesy. His POV; the sting of being remembered too well by some and not at all by others.

chapters.title: The Glasshouse Gates
chapters.summary: Yara stands before the derelict glasshouse, now fenced and condemned. Inside the fence, someone is living — a squatter named Odile who knows the building's secrets. His POV; awe curdling into trespass.

chapters.title: Odile
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She has catalogued the glasshouse's surviving plants for years and resents the demolition; she mistakes Yara for a surveyor. The beat is wary alliance forming over shared custodianship.

chapters.title: Summer, 1999
chapters.summary: Deep flashback: the commune's founding idealism — Beatrix planting, Yara cooking, the group's fragile economy of affection. Yara's POV; nostalgia shown honestly, including its self-deceptions.

chapters.title: The Song's First Life
chapters.summary: The night Beatrix wrote the song, performed once around a stove and never again. Yara's POV; tenderness so acute it hurts, foreshadowing everything it will cost.

chapters.title: Power in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: How the commune's leader, Anselm, turned charisma into control — rationing food, punishing dissent. Yara's POV; the slow horror of complicity.

chapters.title: Beatrix Resists
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, past: she organizes members to leave, and asks Yara to come with her. The beat is hope extended like an open hand.

chapters.title: The Lie
chapters.summary: The pivotal flashback: the night of the fire. Yara, cornered by Anselm, gave up Beatrix's escape plan to protect himself; the confrontation sparked the blaze. His POV; shame rendered without excuse.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Told Wrong
chapters.summary: The official story Yara constructed: anonymous tip, tragic accident, Beatrix blamed for negligence. His POV; the mechanics of a lie becoming a career-long architecture.

chapters.title: Present: The First Crack
chapters.summary: Back in the present, Yara begins interviewing former commune members under pretext of a 'heritage piece.' His POV; each conversation tightens the noose of his own deception.

chapters.title: Anselm Now
chapters.summary: Yara finds Anselm elderly, prosperous, and unrepentant, running a wellness retreat. Their meeting is chess. Yara's POV; the beat is power recognizing power and flinching.

chapters.title: Odile's Discovery
chapters.summary: Odile finds Yara's old notebook hidden in the potting shed — including pages about the fire. Her POV; betrayal of a stranger she'd begun to trust.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Fern House
chapters.summary: Odile confronts Yara; he half-confesses, then retreats into justification. Dual tension; the beat is the reader watching him choose the lie again, smaller this time.

chapters.title: Beatrix Learns He's Here
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV: a mutual friend tells her Yara Voss is in the valley. She drives through the night, rehearsing thirty years of things unsaid. The beat is fury braided with longing.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: Beatrix arrives at the glasshouse. The meeting is civil, surgical, devastating — she thanks him coolly for coming 'before they knock it down.' Alternating close POV; the beat is grief wearing politeness.

chapters.title: The Seed Library
chapters.summary: Yara visits Beatrix's seed library; among the drawers he finds a labeled envelope: seeds saved from the glasshouse, dated the week of the fire. His POV; evidence that she carried the place forward alone.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost Her
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, past and present braided: the blacklisting, the years of being the commune's designated villain, the song she could never bear to finish. The beat is endurance without romance.

chapters.title: The Editor Calls
chapters.summary: Yara's editor demands the heritage piece or his column; meanwhile a rival critic sniffs a story about the fire. His POV; the professional scaffolding begins to sway.

chapters.title: Night in the Palm Room
chapters.summary: Yara stays overnight illegally in the glasshouse with Odile's grudging permission; the song plays again on a wind-up radio, and the past floods in whole. His POV; surrender beginning.

chapters.title: Anselm's Offer
chapters.summary: Anselm offers Yara a deal: a glowing profile of the retreat in exchange for silence about the fire's true cause. His POV; temptation articulated perfectly, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: The Second Lie
chapters.summary: Yara drafts the profile. Halfway through, he reads Beatrix's seed labels again and cannot continue. His POV; the body rebelling against the mind's bargains.

chapters.title: Odile's Testimony
chapters.summary: Odile reveals she was a child in the valley in 1999 and saw someone leave the glasshouse gate open the night of the fire — she has waited decades for the truth. Her POV; the beat is the past demanding its witness.

chapters.title: Confession, Drafted
chapters.summary: Yara writes the true account of the fire — not for publication, but addressed to Beatrix. His POV; the hardest writing of his life, stripped of style.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: He reads the confession to Beatrix in the empty palm room. She does not forgive him; she says the truth is 'a door, not a bridge.' Her POV closing; devastation and a sliver of air.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Yara publishes the confession as his final column, ending his career deliberately. His POV; terror and lightness in equal measure.

chapters.title: Anselm Strikes Back
chapters.summary: Anselm threatens litigation; allies abandon Yara; the town splits. Multi-POV vignettes; the beat is the price of survival finally itemized.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: At a council hearing on the demolition, Yara argues not to save the building but to save its archive and let the rest fall. His POV; wisdom learned late.

chapters.title: Beatrix Sings
chapters.summary: At a small gathering in the glasshouse, Beatrix finishes the song at last — adding the verse she couldn't write until now. Her POV; catharsis without absolution.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: The machines arrive. Yara, Beatrix, and Odile watch together as the glass comes down, salvaging what they carry out by hand. Shared POV; elegy and release.

chapters.title: The Taste of Rain
chapters.summary: In the rubble's dust, rain begins, and Yara tastes it — sour, mineral, unmistakable. His POV; the senses returning not as reward but as consequence.

chapters.title: Inventory, Amended
chapters.summary: Yara burns his old notebook of unsaid things and starts a new page with three true sentences. His POV; the accounting finally balanced.

chapters.title: Seeds
chapters.summary: Beatrix gives him an envelope of glasshouse tomato seeds; he plants them in a borrowed city plot. Alternating POV; the beat is belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What Remains Standing
chapters.summary: One year later: Yara writes a short, honest review of a modest neighborhood kitchen; Beatrix's song circulates, credited; the archive opens in the town library. Closing ensemble POV; the beat is quiet, durable repair.
